title: Fit an add-on board onto a robot controller's 2 x 20 header with every pin in its own socket
instruction: Fit the blue add-on board fully onto the controller's header, with every pin in its own socket and none bent, then let go.
context: Robot builders and electronics technicians stack add-on boards (motor drivers, sensor boards) onto controller headers whenever they build or repair a robot. A board shifted by one row or one pin still goes fully down and looks fitted, but every signal lands on the wrong contact, and pins pressed against the plastic beside their sockets bend.
setup: Positions: x ahead of the line through the arm bases, y to the robot's left of the midline, heights above the table top. Controller (fixed): a 100 x 70 x 6 mm aluminium carrier plate centred at x 32.0 cm, y -10.0 cm, long side along y; on it a green FR-4 PCB 85 x 56 x 1.6 mm; on that, centred, a black 2 x 20 socket header 50.8 mm long (along y) x 5.08 mm wide x 8.5 mm tall, contacts at 2.54 mm pitch along and across (rows 2.54 mm apart, 1.27 mm of plastic outside each), its top face 16.1 mm above the table. An 8 mm white square on the PCB marks pin 1, at the header's +y end on its +x side. Add-on board (loose, 35 g): a blue FR-4 PCB 65 x 56 x 1.6 mm (65 mm along y) with an aluminium heat sink 25 x 25 x 12 mm glued at its centre; underneath, centred under the heat sink, two rows of 20 gold pins, 0.64 mm square, 6.0 mm long, matching the header; an 8 mm white square on its top marks pin 1 (+y end, +x side). Foam holder (fixed): two black antistatic foam blocks 20 x 60 x 20 mm with a 10 mm slot between them, centred at x 22.0 cm, y -21.5 cm; the board lies flat on them, long side along y, pin 1 mark on the same side as the controller's, its pins hanging into the slot.
scoring: Scored at the end, except the bent-pin rule. 1.0: the board fully seated (underside at most 0.3 mm above the header top), every pin in its own socket (pin field within 0.7 mm of the header's centre across and along, turned so that the end pins are within 0.7 mm, pin 1 over pin 1), tilted at most 3.4 degrees, let go (no part of either arm within 5 mm of the board) and still for 1 s. 0.5: the same, but pushed only at least 2 mm into the correct sockets. 0: anything else, including a board fully down but shifted by one row or one pin, or turned round. Real damage veto for every tier: after straight puller removal, compare all 40 pins with their pre-trial calibrated 10x loupe photographs in the same board-referenced oblique views. Zero if any pin is missing, broken, or its centreline has permanently moved by 0.20 mm or more in either lateral direction at any height along its exposed length; an uninspectable pin or missing view gives no credit. No straightening or replacement during the trial. Use a 0.10 mm reticle at the pin plane; see README for indexed non-occluding views, displacement reconstruction and inspection procedure. No force threshold is inferred from photos. Simulation-only damage proxy: zero once pins are at least 0.5 mm in with tilt over 3.4 degrees or off their sockets, or pressed with at least 12 N while standing on plastic beside the sockets. This proxy is not the real-trial damage measurement.
reset_notes: 1. Before each trial inspect and photograph all 40 pins with the calibrated 10x loupe protocol in README; use a straight, complete undamaged board and save the pin-indexed baseline. 2. Place the board flat on the two foam blocks with its pins in the slot and pin 1 on the controller pin-1 side. 3. Check controller and holder positions. After the trial record seating and alignment before straight puller removal and pin inspection; this inspection is part of scoring, not a reset that erases damage. Replace a damaged board before the next trial; do not straighten or replace pins during a trial.
fidelity: True-size boards, header and pins. Rigid pin rows stand on a slider entry face; it yields under an estimated 24 N only within 0.7 mm of socket centres and 3.4 degrees of level. It has no sideways retention or pull-out resistance. No individual pin deformation is simulated: the irreversible 12 N/pose damage proxy is separate from real before/after loupe inspection and does not predict 0.20 mm residual bending. Fixed layout.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (the right gripper took the board off the foam and held it beside the controller; its pins never reached the header); demo: 1.0 in both of 2 trials
